title: VRPAgent: LLM-Driven Discovery of Heuristic Operators for Vehicle Routing Problems

mechanism.domainTask: LLM-driven discovery of destroy and ordering heuristic operators for CVRP, VRPTW, and PCVRP
mechanism.populationDetail: The discovery GA maintains one unpartitioned population of operator-pair implementations; it initializes 100 individuals and subsequent generations comprise 10 elites plus 30 crossover children.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The top 10 individuals form an elite subset retained into the next generation and used for crossover and mutation; the subset is integrated into the population rather than described as a separate external store.
mechanism.replacementDetail: Each individual is a paired implementation of the removal and ordering operators. The population update is generational with elite preservation, and improved mutations can replace individual elites before reassignment.
mechanism.generationDetail: The system initializes operator pairs from scratch, creates offspring by LLM-mediated fusion of one elite and one non-elite parent, and locally mutates each elite using a randomly selected mutation prompt.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: Scalar fitness (average routing objective plus code-length penalty) determines elite rank and is conveyed as better/worse parent status for crossover.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Each crossover pairs one uniformly sampled elite with one uniformly sampled non-elite; mutation uses one elite parent. The elite/non-elite content bias in crossover (80/20) is not a parent-selection probability.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/VRPAGENT LLM-DRIVEN DISCOVERY OF HEURISTIC OPERATORS FOR VEHICLE ROUTING PROBLEMS.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: The survey's multi-elite/archive placement is broadly supported, but the top-k elite subset is integrated into the GA population rather than a separate external archive. Crossover correctly has two true parents; elite mutation has one. Six foundation models are compared across separate runs, not used as a concurrent multi-model architecture. The current survey does not directly cite VRPAgent under prompt structure, replacement mechanisms, foundation-model settings, evaluation feedback, or exploration-exploitation; the paper may support some of these placements, especially its fixed crossover/mutation exploration-exploitation design. Generation-mechanism placement should retain both crossover fusion and elite mutation, with initial generation-from-scratch as initialization.
